title: Pre-Engineered Single-Stair Plan Sets
one_liner: License stamped, fire-marshal-ready plan sets for 4-6 story single-stair buildings so small developers can use the new law without a $250K custom design.
customer: Small infill developers, church and nonprofit landowners and small architecture firms in single-stair states, plus modular fabricators.
problem: Seven states reformed single-stair rules in 2025 and Michigan followed in July 2026, promising about 10% cost savings, but architects and fire officials lack templates. Custom design is slow, local amendments add friction, and construction inputs are up 8.9% while multifamily starts fall.
solution: Engineered plan sets (4/5/6-story, 16-40 units, light-frame and mass-timber variants) with structure and MEP, a fire-safety compensation package, code narrative and a pre-meeting deck for local fire marshals. A network of local architects of record adapts them per site, and a per-state cost estimate is included.
why_now: New laws are taking effect (Michigan July 2026) and California AB 2074 awaits signature, while rising costs make small builders desperate for certainty.
revenue_model: $25-45K per plan license, $10-20K adaptation fee, referral fees from lenders and contractors, and a subscription for code updates.
non_obvious_insight: Legalization does not build housing; templates and fire-marshal comfort do. The first stamped precedent in each state becomes the local pattern, and plan sets have near-zero marginal cost.
first_30_days: Partner with a licensed architect who has single-stair experience. Draft one 4-story 16-unit set for Michigan. Presell three licenses to small developers at a $15K founder price and schedule a meeting with one fire marshal.

title: A Marketplace for Canal Capacity, Not Water
one_liner: A scheduling and capacity-release board that lets irrigation districts sell idle canal and wheeling capacity so conserved or recharge water can physically move to buyers.
customer: Irrigation districts and mutual ditch companies with spare conveyance capacity (sellers), plus growers, groundwater agencies, cities and conservation buyers who need water moved (buyers). Districts pay a subscription and buyers pay per acre-foot wheeled.
problem: Everyone is building marketplaces for water rights and acre-feet. In Western practice the binding constraint is often the ability and permission to move water: capacity, wheeling agreements, losses, turnout scheduling. Idle capacity sits unused while buyers cannot get water delivered. Districts handle wheeling requests by phone and spreadsheet.
solution: Wedge: a shared capacity calendar and wheeling-request workflow for districts, with loss accounting and standard agreements. Then a capacity-release market, like the gas-pipeline capacity release model. The ditch-company share ledger (shares, assessments, transfer approvals) is phase two. Start with one region where transfers already happen.
why_now: The 2027-2036 Colorado River framework and corporate buyers like Amazon create conserved water that must be moved. California groundwater rules and canal capacity loss to subsidence make wheeling scarce. Cheap LoRa gate sensors and open flow gauges make district digitization affordable.
revenue_model: $10-40k/yr district SaaS, plus $5-15 per acre-foot wheeled (roughly 3-5% of price).
non_obvious_insight: Price discovery is missing for the pipes, not the water. Whoever runs the capacity ledger sees every buyer, seller and route, and that data is the moat for every later water market product.
first_30_days: Interview 10 district managers and ditch riders and find one that handles recurring wheeling requests manually. Ship a free shared calendar and request workflow to that district using off-the-shelf tools. Agree that the district will pay per wheeled acre-foot at season end. Publish a public canal-capacity map from open gauge data as top-of-funnel.

title: Group Apprenticeship Employer for Data-Center Electricians
one_liner: An Australian-style group training organization that employs apprentices and rents them to small electrical and plumbing contractors, absorbing the paperwork, wage risk and poaching risk.
customer: Small and mid-size electrical, plumbing and HVAC contractors (5-50 staff) in data-center and construction-boom metros; apprentices, including underemployed college grads.
problem: Electricians have about 72.7k openings a year, boosted by data-center demand, but the 4-5 year path is bottlenecked by employer sponsors and pre-apprenticeship screening. Small contractors cannot carry multi-year risk, admin and classroom scheduling, and apprentices are poached after year one or two. Meanwhile 42% of recent grads are underemployed and have no route in.
solution: The group sponsor is the registered-apprenticeship sponsor and employer of record. It screens and recruits, pays wages and workers' comp, rotates apprentices across host contractors, schedules related instruction with a community college or JATC (up to 49% of instruction can be outsourced to employers or unions under the new apprenticeship rules), and bills hosts hourly. Market a career-changer track to laid-off grads.
why_now: AI data-center construction is pulling electricians while AI is closing entry-level white-collar doors, creating both demand and a motivated recruit pool. Workforce Pell gives apprenticeship-linked programs a fast lane, making college partners eager.
revenue_model: A 20-30% markup over apprentice wage cost billed to host contractors (about 15-20% gross margin, staffing-style), plus state apprenticeship incentives and college partnership fees.
non_obvious_insight: Contractors do not lack applicants; they lack appetite for multi-year risk and administration. Splitting the employer role from the host job site removes the constraint, as group training organizations did in Australia.
first_30_days: Choose one data-center metro. Sign 5 small contractors to LOIs for 10 apprentice seats. Partner with an existing IEC or ABC chapter for registration and compliance. Recruit 30 candidates from local underemployed grads and start an 8-week evening pre-apprenticeship course.

title: Public Toilets as a Stipend Program, Not Construction
one_liner: A turnkey program manager that lets cities and business districts turn cafes, gyms, garages and gas stations into paid, insured and mapped public restrooms for a small annual stipend instead of building $225,000 freestanding toilets.
customer: Business improvement districts and downtown associations first (fast, budgeted, small contracts), then transit agencies, parks and public-works departments, and tourism boards.
problem: Public restrooms are a top complaint in every city and almost no one builds them because the capital and upkeep are brutal. One Portland Loo costs about $225,000 installed, and New York's 2026 pilot budgets about $4M for 17 units. Washington DC authorized a program to pay businesses to open their restrooms in 2018, but it went unfunded. Meanwhile there is a toilet on nearly every retail block behind a 'customers only' sign, because owners fear liability, cleaning cost and misuse, and nobody manages the risk.
solution: Run a managed 'Open Door' network. Recruit and contract the host businesses, pay a monthly stipend, provide a group liability rider or indemnity through a specialty insurance program, supply cleaning kits and signage, and put a QR code and map listing on each door. QR scans verify actual use, so cities pay for measured access and get council-ready reports on use by neighborhood and hour. A hotline handles complaints and revokes hosts who stop complying.
why_now: New York's very public 2026 pilot, including the 10-minute limit robotoilets, shows both political demand and sticker shock. Downtown business districts are fighting for foot traffic, homelessness and tourism pressure keeps restrooms a front-page issue, and smartphone QR verification makes pay-for-access measurable for the first time. Germany's Nette Toilette program has run in about 210 cities for years at roughly $34-$112 a month per business, so the model is proven but has not been productized in the US.
revenue_model: Program-management contract with the city or district: a setup fee plus about $600-$1,200 per site per year, with host stipends passed through at cost. A typical pilot of 15-20 sites is roughly $25-$60k a year. Add sponsorship by a host or utility brand and analytics subscriptions for tourism and transit boards.
non_obvious_insight: The expense of a public toilet is capital and ownership, not access. The scarce resource is liability-managed permission to use toilets that already exist. Whoever builds the group insurance, verification data and host-compliance system owns the market, and every city compares a $2,000-a-year stipend to a $225,000 kiosk.
first_30_days: Target two business improvement districts, which can approve $20-$50k pilots without a city-wide procurement cycle. Sign letters of intent from 15-20 hosts on the strongest blocks. Get a broker to quote a group liability rider. Print door stickers, build a one-page map with scan counts, and launch a 90-day pilot. Use week-4 scan data to ask the district to sign a 12-month contract and to open talks with the city.

title: FEOC and Cyber Passport for Batteries
one_liner: A serial-number-level ledger of material-assistance content and firmware and comms attestations for storage projects, built for tax-credit buyers and insurers.
customer: C&I and utility-scale storage developers and integrators, tax-credit transfer buyers (banks and insurers), and lenders.
problem: FEOC rules require 55% non-FEOC content for storage starting construction in 2026, rising to 75% by 2030. About 80% of US cells are Chinese and non-compliant projects run about 43% pricier. IRS cost tables are not due until 2027, so nobody can prove compliance. Buyers of tax credits and insurers need evidence, and concern about undocumented radios in imported inverters adds a cyber layer.
solution: A workflow and ledger that captures the bill of materials at cell and module level with supplier attestations and cost tables, then computes the material-assistance ratio conservatively. Each project gets an audit-ready evidence packet. Optional teardown, RF and firmware attestation runs through a partner lab. The 'passport' is what transfer buyers and insurers accept.
why_now: FEOC applies to 2026 construction starts, the tax-credit transfer market is doing diligence at scale, and tariffs are rising.
revenue_model: $15-50k per project, $2-5k a month SaaS per developer, verification fees from transfer buyers, and cost-plus lab attestation.
non_obvious_insight: The burden is evidence, not sourcing. With IRS guidance missing, the first firm whose conservative methodology gets accepted becomes the de facto standard, and insurers will only underwrite recapture cover against that record.
first_30_days: Publish a free MACR calculator with conservative assumptions. Interview 10 developers and three tax-credit transfer buyers. Sell three paid compliance-file builds at ~$15k for 2026-start projects. Pre-agree terms with an attestation lab.

title: Tariff Surcharge Clawback for Downstream Buyers
one_liner: A contingency recovery-audit firm that claws back tariff surcharges buyers paid on duties their suppliers have since had refunded.
customer: CFOs, AP and purchasing teams at $20M-$1B manufacturers and distributors that paid itemized supplier 'tariff surcharges' in 2025-26.
problem: The Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20. By 2026-07-10 CBP had accepted about $121.75B in claims and repaid about $86.3B. Many suppliers billed explicit surcharges (one shop-floor post cites 2.7%) to fund those duties, and they are now collecting refunds on the same money. Buyers assume the refund belongs to the importer of record, and AP treats surcharge lines as noise.
solution: Ingest 18 months of AP data from the ERP or QuickBooks. Use LLM extraction on invoices and price-increase emails to find surcharge lines. Rank suppliers by likely refunded exposure (product HTS and the IEEPA rate window). Generate credit-memo demands and negotiation scripts. Escalate to counsel only for large amounts. Recovery depends on invoice and contract language, and most cases settle as credits against future invoices.
why_now: Refunds are paying out in phases right now, so suppliers hold the cash today. Contract dispute windows are open and evidence is fresh.
revenue_model: 20-30% contingency fee on recovered cash or credits. Optional $5k flat fee for a scan of the last 12 months of AP.
non_obvious_insight: The strongest and cheapest claim to a refund often belongs to the downstream buyer holding an itemized surcharge, not the importer. Recovery-audit firms hunt duplicate payments, not tariffs. Buyers also avoid asking for fear of damaging the supplier relationship, so an anonymous third party has an edge.
first_30_days: Sign 5 mid-market manufacturers for a free 12-month surcharge scan. Have counsel draft one template letter. Send the first demands and measure realized recovery. First credit memos should land within 60-90 days.

title: Side-Selling Early Warning for Milk and Coffee Coops
one_liner: A churn-prediction and targeted-advance service that tells dairy and coffee cooperatives which farmers are about to side-sell to cash brokers, and triggers the right cash intervention before the volume walks away.
customer: Managers and boards of medium-sized dairy cooperatives (about 2,000-10,000 farmers), coffee cooperative societies and factories, and mid-sized processors that buy from farmer groups. They pay because lost throughput hits fixed factory costs and credit recovery.
problem: Side-selling is the silent killer of Kenyan coops. Farmers sell milk to hawkers and raw-milk traders, or coffee cherry to cash buyers, who pay on the spot, while the coop pays monthly or later and then deducts for feeds, inputs, AI services and loans. Deliveries fade slowly, not suddenly, so managers notice too late. Side-selling spikes when a farmer's net pay is squeezed by deductions, when payment is late, or in cash-crunch weeks such as January and other school fee dates, funerals and sickness. Coops respond with lectures and warnings instead of predicting and fixing the cash gap.
solution: Ingest the coop's delivery and payment history (usually already exported from the weighing or dairy management software). A simple gradient-boosted or rule-based model scores each farmer weekly for side-selling risk using delivery drift, missed pay days, deductions as a share of gross, days since last payment, seasonality and school-term calendars. The coop gets a daily short list for its field officer, with SMS or voice-call scripts in the local language. The intervention is a coop-funded, capped advance or deduction holiday for at-risk farmers in their predicted cash-crunch window, since the coop already holds the delivered stock and the farmer's record as collateral. It measures recovered litres or kilos against a control group.
why_now: Global arabica prices spiked to record highs in 2025 and pulled cherry towards cash brokers in Kenya, at the same time as coffee-sector reforms push coops to pay faster and more transparently. Weighing scales and dairy management software have digitised delivery data at many coops over the last five years, so the data now exists. M-Pesa bulk disbursement makes weekly or on-demand advances cheap. Modern ML tooling makes a credible model a two-week job rather than a research project. I could not verify current legal specifics, so confirm the latest coffee and dairy regulations and data-protection obligations (coop as data controller) before pilots.
revenue_model: Performance fee of roughly 5-10% of recovered volume value (paid from the additional milk or cherry that stays in the coop), or a SaaS retainer of a few tens of thousands of shillings per month per coop. Later, licensing the model to processors and lenders who want a farmer reliability signal.
non_obvious_insight: Side-selling is not disloyalty, it is a rational response to cash-flow timing. The winning intervention is not a scolding letter but a small advance placed at the right moment, funded by the coop's own working capital. It is also predictable from delivery patterns weeks before it happens, because farmers taper deliveries before they stop. Most agritech sells farmers new products, whereas here the buyer is the institution that quietly loses 10% or more of its volume.
first_30_days: Get 24 months of delivery and payment CSVs from one or two coops, ideally through your own parents' society or the manager you know personally. Build the risk model in a notebook, deliver a top-200 at-risk list plus a script, and run a 60-day test where half the list gets the SMS and advance offer and half does not. Agree to be paid only on retained volume compared to the control group, and use the result as the case study for the next five coops.

title: Escrow and Tax Rails for Agent-Hired Humans
one_liner: The compliance and payment layer that lets software agents legally hire humans for judgment and real-world tasks: owner KYC, task-legality screening, escrow, worker classification and tax forms.
customer: Agent-framework developers and companies whose agents need on-call humans (verification, phone calls, notarisation, in-person checks), plus the workers doing the tasks. Take rate is 8-12%.
problem: Agent-to-human marketplaces are appearing (47jobs, Hirenewtalent.ai in the brief, and viral 'rent a human' sites in early 2026), but nobody is the clear payor, employer or liable party. Who issues 1099s, who is responsible if an agent sends someone to do something illegal or never pays, and how do workers avoid scams?
solution: An API plus MCP tool ('ask_human'): agents post tasks against funded escrow tied to a KYC'd human or company principal. A legality and safety classifier rejects risky tasks. Automatic tax forms and classification, dispute arbitration and two-sided reputation follow, with optional injury insurance for physical tasks.
why_now: Agent frameworks and MCP matured in 2025, agent-payment standards and stablecoin rails are being rolled out, and agent-run marketplaces are going viral. Regulators will demand a principal of record after the first scandal.
revenue_model: 8-12% take rate on tasks plus an insurance margin for physical work.
non_obvious_insight: The marketplace is cheap to clone. The moat is the principal-of-record and liability layer, which is what regulators and enterprise buyers will eventually require, so building the compliant rails first wins the boring middle.
first_30_days: Ship a minimal escrow API and MCP tool with 200 vetted workers in one niche (phone verification calls, document notarisation, local checks in 3 cities). Onboard 10 agent builders through Discord and HN and complete the first 500 paid tasks.

title: Independent Audits for Per-Outcome Agent Invoices
one_liner: The DoubleVerify of AI agents: sample and verify the resolutions, meetings and approvals you were billed for, then claim credits for the fakes.
customer: Finance, procurement and support-ops leaders at companies paying $50k-$5M a year to outcome-priced agent vendors (support resolutions, AP processing, claims, scheduling).
problem: Vendors have moved from seats to outcomes. Reportedly, Zendesk narrowed billing to LLM-verified 'resolutions' at about $1.20-$1.50 each and HubSpot's customer agent charges about $0.50 per resolved conversation. The vendor defines and grades its own outcome, and buyers cannot tell a real resolution from a customer who gave up. Step two of falling token prices is vendors with an incentive to over-count outcomes.
solution: A read-only connector to the buyer's helpdesk, CRM or ERP that re-derives outcomes independently from reopen rates, repeat contacts in 7-14 days, silent abandonment, escalation to humans and sentiment. Sample about 300 outcomes a month for blind human plus LLM review. Deliver a monthly invoice integrity report with the false-outcome rate and a credit-claim packet aligned to the contract's dispute window.
why_now: Outcome pricing became mainstream in 2026, and Deloitte published guidance in June 2026 on accounting for it, which signals CFO attention. Buyers paying per outcome have no independent measurement.
revenue_model: 10-20% of credits recovered plus a $2-6k/month subscription. The buy side pays first to avoid conflict, and vendors may later pay for an audited badge.
non_obvious_insight: Ad tech showed that when sellers measure their own outcomes, a third-party verifier becomes a category (DoubleVerify, IAS). Agent outcome pricing recreates that conflict with almost no independent measurement, and the earliest data is anonymous benchmarks of false-resolution rates.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 companies using Fin, Zendesk or HubSpot agents through support-ops communities. Run a free or contingency retrospective audit of 3 months of invoices and publish anonymized false-resolution rates to seed demand.

title: Hazmat Sidecar for Small Old-House Repairs
one_liner: A flat-price, same-week asbestos and lead test-and-remove service that solo-to-five-tech plumbing, HVAC, electrical and flooring shops call when a small job in a pre-1980 house hits suspect material, with the waste manifest handled for them.
customer: Small trade shops (pay per call and pass through) and homeowners; property managers are a later segment.
problem: Median home age is 44 years and 62% of homeowners now choose repair over replace, so small jobs constantly disturb duct wrap, vinyl tile, transite, plaster and lead paint. Licensed abatement firms impose $2-5K minimums and weeks of lead time, so contractors either walk away (feeding the 73% project backlog) or cut corners and carry liability. Few landfills accept asbestos waste, and manifests and pre-notification confuse small shops.
solution: A van with two accredited techs: same-week sample results through a partner lab, flat-fee minor removal where state rules allow (subcontracted where they don't), bagged, labeled and manifested disposal, and a digital clearance letter the trade can hand the homeowner. Shops book by text and can subscribe for priority.
why_now: Repair-over-replace, tariff-inflated equipment and HVAC's 2025 shipment trough leave small shops chasing any billable job and unwilling to lose one to a hazmat surprise. Larger platforms (ServiceTitan, PE roll-ups) do not serve sub-$10K jobs.
revenue_model: $300-1,500 per job; per-sample testing fees; $99/mo priority subscription for trade shops.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not removal labor but the disposal chain: manifests, landfill acceptance and pollution insurance. Owning that chain lets one small team become the referral default for every trade in the area.
first_30_days: Days 1-30: complete state inspector accreditation, lead-safe firm certification and worker courses, get a pollution-liability quote and sign a landfill acceptance agreement. Meanwhile pre-sign 10 trade shops to a flat-price menu. Days 30-90: run the first 20 jobs and refine pricing.

title: Convert Legacy RPA Bots Using Their Own Logs
one_liner: Use years of bot execution logs as free ground-truth tests to convert brittle RPA bots into monitored agents at a fixed price per bot.
customer: Mid-market companies (500-10,000 employees) with 20-300 UiPath, Blue Prism or Power Automate bots in finance ops, claims and HR, plus RPA consultancies as a channel.
problem: Vendor and consultancy estimates put RPA upkeep at several times license cost, and UI changes break bots constantly. Leaders want agents but fear regression, and migration advice is generic ('retire the brittle ones first'). RPA vendors are pivoting to agentic pitches themselves, which increases pressure without giving a safe method.
solution: Ingest bot definitions and run logs, replay historical inputs to a candidate agent, and differentially test its outputs against the bot's recorded outputs. Cut over each bot when parity passes a threshold, keep the old bot in shadow for 30 days, monitor for drift, and price per bot converted plus a run-and-monitor fee.
why_now: Computer-use agents can operate UIs reliably enough to compete with scripted bots, and RPA vendors are moving to orchestration. Budgets are earmarked because maintenance costs are visible.
revenue_model: $2-$6k per bot conversion plus $200-$500/month per bot run and monitoring, with revenue share for consultancy partners.
non_obvious_insight: The hard part of migrating automations is knowing the new one is right. Legacy bots have already produced years of labeled input-output pairs for free, which turns migration into differential testing.
first_30_days: Find 10 mid-market RPA shops and ask each for 5 brittle bots. Convert 5 bots across 2 customers in shadow mode, show parity, and sign a fixed-fee conversion for the next 20.

title: Compute Boilers: Servers That Heat Buildings
one_liner: Install liquid-cooled inference servers in the boiler rooms of hotels, dorms, pools and laundries, sell the compute, and give the building cheap hot water.
customer: Hotels, university housing, municipal pools and YMCAs, multifamily buildings with central hot water, and laundries. They get cheaper heat. Inference providers buy the compute.
problem: Large AI sites wait years in interconnection queues, yet buildings already have continuous thermal loads, existing 3-phase service and unused headroom. Sub-MW loads avoid large-load studies. Owners face pressure to electrify hot water and building-emissions fines such as NYC's Local Law 97.
solution: Sealed 30-100 kW direct-to-chip liquid-cooled modules plumbed into building hot-water loops that capture most of the heat. The company owns and operates the hardware and sells GPU-hours to inference customers through a neocloud partner. The host gets heat at a discount to its gas or electric cost. First product: 20-40 kW pilots at about 10 hotels and pools in one metro.
why_now: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling is now standard, AI demand exceeds grid supply, small-model inference fits ordinary fiber, and UK pool and hot-water-cylinder server projects prove the model.
revenue_model: Compute revenue share, heat sold to hosts at 50-70% of their current fuel cost, and GPU-lender financing of the hardware.
non_obvious_insight: The grid is not short of electrons. It is short of interconnection at big sites. Sub-MW building sites already have service and a thermal sink, and heat reuse lowers hosting cost below any standalone data center, so the queue is bypassed.
first_30_days: Sign LOIs with five hospitality or pool operators in a state with cheap power and good fiber. Run heat-load audits. Spec a module with a liquid-cooling OEM. Get a GPU-lender term sheet. Deploy a 10 kW test unit at one site.

title: Verified-Outreach Ledger for Government and Utilities
one_liner: A system where police, courts, tax offices and utilities log every outbound contact so residents can confirm in 20 seconds that they really called.
customer: County sheriffs and police departments, court clerks, county tax collectors, municipal utilities, and state benefits offices, buying through state cooperative contracts. Banks' fraud teams later.
problem: Law-enforcement impersonation drew about 61,000 complaints and $1.6B+ from Jan 2025 to Jul 2026, now with AI and fake video calls. The public message is 'the government never calls, hang up', which makes real outreach (jury duty, warrant notices, benefits recertification, shutoff notices) fail. Honest institutions can no longer reach people.
solution: Staff log each outreach in a lightweight tool or via CAD/CRM integration, and each contact gets a short code read aloud. Residents verify by calling or texting a verification number or visiting a page on the agency's .gov domain, which confirms agency, staffer, purpose and callback line. It also supports missed-contact reports and a library of 'we will never ask' scripts, and logs scam attempts for reporting.
why_now: The FBI's Sep 17 2026 PSA on law-enforcement impersonation makes the pain current, and video-call impersonation defeats 'just check the caller' advice. Google's on-device scam detection helps only one channel. Agencies have grant money for fraud outreach.
revenue_model: $3-12K per year per small agency via cooperative purchasing, $30-50K for a county-wide deployment, and per-message fees for banks and utilities.
non_obvious_insight: The second-order damage of the scam wave is trust deflation. Every warning that trains people to distrust callers makes legitimate callers less effective. The fix is to make the legitimate caller provable, not chase the fraudulent one.
first_30_days: Build a simple web tool plus a Twilio verification line in two weeks. Pilot with 3 sheriff's offices and one county court via a state sheriffs' association at $250 per month, and have them include codes on real warrant and jury notices.

title: Callback Verification Network for Invoice-Paying Agents
one_liner: A consortium ledger of verified vendor bank details plus automated out-of-band callbacks that gives accounts-payable agents a signed safe-to-pay attestation before they send money to changed payment instructions.
customer: Bookkeeping and AP-outsourcing firms (each managing 100-300 SMB clients) and AP-automation vendors first, then mid-market controllers ($50M-$1B revenue).
problem: Business email compromise costs roughly $2.8B a year in reported US losses. Humans used to catch odd bank-detail changes by accident, but an AP agent that reads emails and PDFs will follow an instruction injected into an invoice at machine speed (prompt injection maps to 6 of 10 OWASP agentic risks). The US has no Confirmation of Payee, unlike the UK (since 2020) and the EU (Verification of Payee mandated from October 2025).
solution: An API the AP agent calls whenever bank details are new or changed. We match against a shared ledger of callback-verified details contributed by all customers, run TIN and account-ownership checks, and if still unverified place an outbound voice-agent call to the number on file from the last verified contract or W-9, never the number on the invoice. We return a signed attestation that the payment policy requires, and anything unattested routes to a human. An optional guarantee covers attested payments.
why_now: Agentic AP is shipping in 2026, Nacha's 2026 fraud-monitoring rule phases push originators to prove controls, Google's threat group documents autonomous multi-agent credential harvesting in under 6 hours, and voice agents make a verification callback cost cents instead of a clerk's ten minutes.
revenue_model: $3-8 per new-or-changed-details verification, $0.15-0.40 per payment monitored, and a guarantee premium (about 1-3 bps of attested payment value) once loss data exists.
non_obvious_insight: Agents remove the accidental friction that used to stop fraud, so the defense that works is a channel the attacker and any injected prompt cannot touch. A shared ledger strengthens with every adopter, which builds Confirmation of Payee bottom-up in a country whose banks will not build it.
first_30_days: Sign 10 bookkeeping firms that together manage 1,000+ SMB vendors. Run callbacks semi-manually with a voice agent and humans on escalation, and sell a verified-vendor book at $99 per month per client. Wire a webhook into one AP tool (Bill.com or Ramp style) so the attestation gates payment approval.

title: Asset Provenance Ledger for AI Disclosure
one_liner: A plugin for Blender, Photoshop, Unity and Unreal that logs where each asset came from (human-made, AI-generated, purchased) and exports evidence for Steam disclosure and award eligibility.
customer: Indie and mid-size studios (5-100 staff) shipping on Steam, and awards and festival organizers who must adjudicate AI use.
problem: Clair Obscur lost two Indie Game Awards over AI placeholder textures removed before shipping. Eurogamer scored ARC Raiders 2/5 partly over AI voices. Valve requires AI disclosure on Steam. Accusations arrive after launch and the accused have no evidence trail either way.
solution: A local-first logger records per-asset origin (DCC commit hooks, generative-tool API logs, asset-store IDs) into a signed hash chain. It exports an AI Disclosure Report for Steam, award submissions and press, and offers a verifier portal for juries and a public provenance page.
why_now: Award controversies and press scoring now turn on AI use. Steam's disclosure requirement is in force. EA's owners plan AI throughout operations, which will multiply cases.
revenue_model: $15-49 per seat per month, $2-5k per event for awards verification, and $3-10k for forensic audits of accused studios.
non_obvious_insight: The dispute is not AI versus human, it is evidence asymmetry: accusers need no proof and the accused have none. A provenance log protects studios that use AI legitimately (placeholders, disclosed tools) as much as those that do not.
first_30_days: Ship a minimal Blender, Photoshop and Unity logger. Offer it free to awards-eligible entries. Talk to organizers of two indie awards about a verifier pilot, and onboard 20 studios.

title: Recurring-Route Repricing Desk for Service Owners
one_liner: Read-only connect a lawn, pool, cleaning or pest route to its books, find the customers who are losing money, and hand the owner ready-to-send price-increase letters.
customer: Owners of 2-15 person recurring-service companies (lawn, pool, cleaning, pest, window) on Jobber, Housecall Pro or ServiceM8 plus QuickBooks. They pay a one-time audit fee, then a monthly retainer.
problem: Owners discover their margin problem after the fact. r/sweatystartup: "Profitable jobs on paper keep turning into break-even or worse when I look at the actual numbers after" (82/100). A Jobber Community thread is titled "Anyone else realize they were breaking even or losing money after expenses?", and its owner had a full schedule but jobs barely broke even once true payroll burden (taxes, workers comp), supplies, insurance and transaction fees were counted. Tools do not fix it: Jobber adds job costing only on its $39-199/mo plans, and Joist stops at $8/mo estimates. Fear of losing the client keeps owners from raising prices.
solution: 1) A read-only connection or CSV export of Jobber or Housecall Pro, QuickBooks or Stripe, and payroll. 2) Per-customer true margin, including labor burden, drive time, card fees and callbacks. 3) A ranked list of customers to raise by X%, re-scope or drop. 4) Auto-drafted price-increase notices, phone scripts and rebuttals for the "I'll go elsewhere" reply. 5) A churn tracker that shows what each increase cost or earned. It is sold as a productized service backed by software, not as a dashboard.
why_now: Owners are absorbing cost increases in labor, insurance and materials and cannot afford to keep pricing by feel. LLMs let a two-person team parse messy exports and receipts and allocate costs per customer, which used to take a bookkeeper hours. Incumbent field-service tools keep gating job costing behind upper tiers.
revenue_model: $149 one-time margin audit. $99-199/mo retainer for monthly re-scoring, letters and churn tracking. Optional 10% referral to insurers or payroll partners.
non_obvious_insight: Every field-service tool records revenue. The missing piece is cost allocation and the nerve to raise prices, so the paid deliverable is the letter and the script, not another dashboard. Evidence: r/sweatystartup cluster "Unprofitable Service Jobs" and "How do you price your cleaning jobs? Looking to update my rates" (https://www.ideafast.pro/pains/sweatystartup). The owner-facing forum thread is at https://community.getjobber.com/discussions/finances-forum/anyone-else-realize-they-were-breaking-even-or-losing-money-after-expenses/9694. Job costing is gated to $39-199/mo tiers and estimate tools stop at $8/mo (https://www.microgaps.com/blog/saas-niches-nobody-talking-about-2026). r/smallbusiness shows the fear: "Should I fire a client that's 50% of my revenue?" and "Client sent me a 1-star review because I charged for extra work" (https://www.ideafast.pro/pains/smallbusiness). SaaS is structurally a poor fit for tiny businesses, so a service with custom tooling wins here (https://beekeycheung.substack.com/p/saas-products-leave-small-businesses).
first_30_days: Week 1: post in r/sweatystartup and the Jobber Community offering 10 free margin audits from a CSV export. Weeks 2-3: do them by hand in a spreadsheet and record which customers each owner would raise or drop. Week 4: convert to $149 audits and pre-sell the $99/mo retainer to the first 5. Target 20 paid audits and 5 retainers within the first two months.

title: Alpha-Gal-Safe Pharmacy With Verified Ingredient Sourcing
one_liner: A cash-pay pharmacy and lookup service that tells tick-allergy (alpha-gal) patients which pill in their cabinet is safe, by NDC and lot, and compounds the ones that are not.
customer: Adults with alpha-gal syndrome, who pay cash for a membership and for compounded fills. CDC estimates up to 450,000 people were affected in 2010-2022, concentrated in the Southeast, Midwest and mid-Atlantic and spreading. A second wave of buyers is allergy clinics, health-system pharmacies and hospital perioperative teams, who would pay a license fee for the database.
problem: Drug makers are not required to disclose whether gelatin, glycerin, magnesium stearate or heparin came from a mammal. The label says 'gelatin' and nothing more. The free Alpha-gal Information (AGI) mammalian byproducts database works at ingredient level, not for the exact NDC and lot in the patient's hand. A pharmacist verifying one drug spends 30-90 minutes calling manufacturers. Then the wholesaler switches generic suppliers, the excipients change silently, and a patient who has been stable for a year ends up with anaphylaxis or a 2 a.m. ER visit. Patients and their Facebook groups crowd-source this by hand.
solution: 1) Build an NDC-level sourcing ledger. A pharmacist team sends templated requests to manufacturers for written excipient-source statements, and an LLM parses the replies and DailyMed SPL excipient lists. Each NDC gets a tier (plant or synthetic confirmed, mammal-derived, unknown) plus the date and lot range. 2) Sell a 'Safe Fill' membership that dispenses only verified NDCs, pins the manufacturer with a do-not-substitute request to the prescriber, and alerts the member when a source changes. 3) Compound unavailable items into HPMC vegetable capsules. This fits the 503A 'significant clinical difference' allowance because a documented allergy is a patient-specific reason, unlike copy compounding. 4) License the ledger to health systems and allergy groups.
why_now: Alpha-gal is now recognized as far more common than clinicians assumed, and the lone star tick's range keeps expanding. Regulators and payers have turned hostile to copy compounding after the 2025 GLP-1 shortage ended, so the legitimate lane is narrow, patient-specific allergy compounding, and this idea sits squarely in it. LLMs make parsing messy manufacturer letters and SPL data feasible for a two-person team, which was not true three years ago.
revenue_model: About $14 a month per patient membership (lookups, sourcing letters, source-change alerts, substitution management). Dispensing and compounding margin on cash-pay fills ($25-60 per compounded fill). B2B database license of $5k-25k a year per health system or allergy group. Optional paid sourcing-verification requests from hospitals for one-off drugs.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not a list of bad ingredients. It is provenance per NDC and lot, which changes silently when a wholesaler swaps a generic supplier, and only the dispensing pharmacist sees the swap happen. Whoever holds a dated, manufacturer-confirmed ledger owns the trust of a patient group that currently does all of this by hand and pays cash for certainty.
first_30_days: Pick the 50 most-prescribed oral drugs plus anticoagulant alternatives. Send NDC-specific inquiry letters to manufacturers and publish a free 'verified so far' list to build search traffic and credibility. Join the alpha-gal patient communities and offer 100 founding members $9 a month for life. A pharmacist owner with a compounding license fills the first cash orders locally. Get a review letter from two allergists. File nonresident pharmacy license applications in the top tick-prevalence states, such as TN, KY, MO, VA, NC and AR.

title: Auracast Hearing Access for Churches and Senior Centers
one_liner: Turnkey Bluetooth Auracast broadcast installs that let people with hearing loss hear services, meetings and group activities directly in their own hearing aids and earbuds.
customer: Houses of worship, senior centers, libraries, community halls and municipal meeting rooms, paying $1.5-6k for install plus $50-150 a month managed service.
problem: Hearing loss is a leading modifiable dementia risk and a quiet driver of withdrawal: people stop going to services, dinners and meetings because they cannot follow. Fewer than one in three adults who could benefit use hearing aids. Legacy hearing loops are costly and often fail unnoticed, and FM systems require borrowing clunky receivers. Venues with amplified sound face ADA assistive-listening obligations that many ignore.
solution: Pre-configured Auracast transmitters (line-in or audio-over-IP) installed in a day, with QR signage ('join the broadcast'), usher training, room-level coverage checks and a remote-monitoring dashboard so it keeps working. Multi-channel support allows a second-language stream (English and Spanish) from the same room.
why_now: Auracast (LE Audio broadcast) is shipping in current hearing aids, phones and earbuds. OTC hearing aids (2022) and AirPods Pro hearing-aid features (Sep-Oct 2024) expanded the user base. Loneliness is now a WHO-measured metric, and venues want visible ways to include older attendees.
revenue_model: Install fee plus recurring managed-service subscription. Referral fees from audiologists and hearing-aid manufacturers seeking demand generation.
non_obvious_insight: The hidden loneliness intervention is upstream of any program: tens of millions of people with hearing loss quietly stop attending. Fixing the room is cheaper than fixing the person, and Auracast collapses the cost of doing it.
first_30_days: Buy three transmitters (about $300-600 each). Install free in three churches or senior centers in one metro with an audiologist partner, capture attendance and testimonials, then sell ten installs at about $2.5k through denominational newsletters and audiologist referrals.

title: Managed 24-Hour CRA Vulnerability Reporting Desk
one_liner: A hosted OWASP Dependency-Track plus an on-call analyst rota that tells small hardware makers within hours whether an exploited vulnerability hits their firmware, then drafts the ENISA 24h/72h filings.
customer: EU-selling makers of connected hardware with 5-250 staff and no product-security team (smart-home devices, e-bikes, EV chargers, industrial gateways, toys, wearables). Buyer is the CTO or regulatory/CE-marking manager. Secondary channel is CE-marking consultants who need a white-label reporting partner.
problem: The EU Cyber Resilience Act's reporting duties went live on 11 Sept 2026. Manufacturers must send an early warning within 24 hours of becoming aware of an actively exploited vulnerability, then detail within 72 hours, through ENISA's Single Reporting Platform. Fines reach EUR 15M or 2.5% of turnover. Small makers ship Yocto, OpenWrt, Zephyr, OpenSSL and FFmpeg stacks and often can't say what is inside a firmware image. Nobody on their team is awake on Sunday when a CISA KEV entry lands.
solution: Ingest CycloneDX/SPDX SBOMs into a managed Dependency-Track instance. For products with no SBOM, generate one from the firmware image with Syft, cdxgen or EMBA, using Ghidra for binary-only blobs. Watch CISA KEV, the EU vulnerability database and OSV continuously. A human analyst issues a VEX verdict (affected / not affected / under investigation) within hours. If affected, the desk pre-fills the SRP notification, drafts the customer advisory, and tracks the 24h, 72h and final-report clocks. The output is an auditable VEX history that a market-surveillance authority or notified body can read.
why_now: The 24-hour reporting clock started 11 Sept 2026 and the ENISA platform is open, so thousands of small makers are discovering they have weeks rather than the Dec 2027 date for full application. Dependency-Track and CycloneDX are the de facto open standards, but the paid options are enterprise appsec suites priced far above a 20-person hardware company's budget.
revenue_model: Retainer of EUR 300-1,500 per month per product family, tiered by number of firmware images and response-time SLA. One-off firmware SBOM generation at EUR 2-8k per image. Resale to CE consultants at a wholesale rate. Later add annual CRA technical-file support.
non_obvious_insight: Small manufacturers don't need another scanner, because the open-source plumbing already works. They need a human who can say 'not affected' with evidence inside 24 hours, because a false 'affected' filing is also costly. The scarce asset is analyst judgment plus a growing VEX history, which compounds across customers who share the same upstream components.
first_30_days: Stand up stock Dependency-Track and a KEV/EUVD watcher. Recruit 2-3 freelance embedded-security engineers for a shared on-call rota. Offer 20 free 'CRA exposure scans' (one firmware image in, one-page exposed-CVE report out) to IoT startups and to 100 CE-marking consultants found on LinkedIn and trade forums. Publish a weekly 'which exploited CVEs hit your Yocto/OpenWrt image' digest to build the list. Convert scans into 6-month retainers at a design-partner price.

title: Sell the Route, Not the Business
one_liner: A standardized customer-book sale with a retention earn-out held in escrow and released automatically from payment data.
customer: Owner-operators aged 58+ of recurring-revenue routes with $80-500k revenue (pool, lawn, pest, cleaning, snow, window, HVAC maintenance, small bookkeeping and tax practices), and 5-30 employee competitors nearby who would buy them.
problem: No broker will list a $150k-revenue business, so retiring owners walk away and customers scatter. Buyers can't verify retention and the parties fight over price. Search funds target $5-50M companies and nothing serves the sub-$1M tier.
solution: Package the asset as the recurring customer relationship, not the entity. The product supplies consented customer-list transfer, a standard purchase agreement, a pricing multiple on trailing recurring revenue, and a 12-month retention earn-out held in escrow that releases as Stripe, QuickBooks or bank data confirms customers still pay. It adds customer-notice and handover-ride workflows, a non-compete, and matching to nearby operators. SBA Express lender partners finance the buyer.
why_now: From July 2026 an SBA 7(a) can be combined with a 504 for up to $10M, which loosens acquisition credit. Payment data now makes retention measurable in real time. An aging owner cohort meets flat CPA supply on the bookkeeping side.
revenue_model: 5-8% success fee to seller and buyer, plus escrow and retention-tracking fees, plus referral fees from lenders and insurers.
non_obvious_insight: At this size nobody needs to find a buyer for the business, because the natural buyer is the competitor with trucks two zip codes away. Retention escrow turns the valuation argument into a measured outcome.
first_30_days: Choose one vertical (for example pool routes) in one metro. Broker three deals by hand through Facebook groups and route-broker forums using a lawyer-drafted standard contract and Stripe Connect escrow. Document time to close and retention, then productize the paperwork.

title: Approved-Protocol Envelope Guard for AI-Directed Labs
one_liner: Middleware that turns an institution's biosafety approval into machine-readable limits and stops any agent-proposed experiment that falls outside them before a robot runs it, leaving an insurer-grade black-box record.
customer: Biosafety officers and lab directors at universities, CROs and AI-native biotechs that let agents propose or modify protocols. Later, insurers and MGAs who need trace data. The direct buyer is the lab or institution.
problem: Institutional Biosafety Committees approve specific organisms, agents, quantities and containment levels, but agents now propose edits on the fly (a new strain, a higher concentration, a substitute reagent). There is no standard sign-off model, since CDC/WHO frameworks predate autonomous systems, and records must separate AI proposal, human edit and robot execution. ISO's generative-AI exclusion (CG 40 47 01 26) took effect in January 2026 and Verisk is weighing agentic exclusions, so the resulting liability is increasingly uninsured.
solution: Ingest the approved protocol (IBC registration, BSL level, permitted agents and amounts, IACUC limits) as a machine-readable envelope. Check every agent-proposed step against it before execution. Anything out of envelope pauses the run and goes to the biosafety officer with a diff. All proposals, human edits and executions are logged tamper-evidently. Each run yields an 'envelope compliance report' for the IBC file and, later, for underwriters.
why_now: Anthropic's wet lab and similar setups (about 950 agents on one discovery) show agents can generate far more proposals than human reviewers can read. The FDA's September 2026 nonclinical-methods rule raises scrutiny of AI-run studies. Carriers are excluding what they cannot model, so trace holders can price the risk.
revenue_model: SaaS per lab or robot ($1-3K/month), enterprise deployments for CROs, and later an MGA or data-licensing arrangement in which underwriters pay for envelope-compliance telemetry or grant premium credits.
non_obvious_insight: The real buyer is the overloaded biosafety officer, not the scientist, and the hard part is translating IBC PDFs into constraints rather than the AI. Whoever holds the runtime traces becomes the pricing authority for agentic lab risk, and model labs cannot be that neutral party.
first_30_days: Interview 15 biosafety officers through the ABSA community. Ship a read-only 'diff checker' that takes an IBC protocol PDF plus an agent's experiment plan and flags out-of-envelope steps. Sell 3 paid pilots ($2-5K) to AI-native labs and one university core. Use the pilot logs to draft an insurer-ready report format.

title: Bank-Accepted $1,500 Diligence for Main Street Deals
one_liner: A fixed-price, CPA-signed mini quality-of-earnings pack that brokers attach to sub-$1M business listings so SBA lenders and first-time buyers can close deals that currently die at diligence.
customer: Business brokers listing $150K-$1M cash-flow businesses (pay about $995 per listing to pre-certify), first-time individual buyers (pay $1,500 at letter of intent), and community-bank SBA lenders who accept the format.
problem: Boomer-owned Main Street businesses (HVAC, laundromats, landscaping, small clinics) sell on seller-supplied P&Ls and add-backs because a real quality-of-earnings review costs roughly $15K-50K (prior knowledge), which is more than many deals can bear. Search-fund capital targets $5-50M companies, so no formal capital or diligence product exists below $1M (brief inference). Deals die late or close on bad numbers.
solution: A five-day standardized pack. AI ties out bank feeds, POS data and sales-tax filings to IRS tax transcripts (hard to forge), samples add-backs, checks customer and revenue concentration, runs a reviews-and-traffic authenticity check (bought reviews and followers inflate perceived brand value), scans liens, licenses and litigation, and produces an owner-dependence score. A partner CPA reviews and signs. The signed pack attaches to the listing and is reusable across buyers.
why_now: SBA loosened acquisition financing on 2026-07-04 (7(a) and 504 loans can be combined for up to $10M of SBA-backed financing). AI-forged P&Ls and bank-statement PDFs are now trivial to produce (prior knowledge), so lenders and buyers need evidence that survives forgery. CPA supply is flat at about 678K, so cheap AI tie-out plus a reviewing CPA is the only way to serve small deals. Bench's Dec 2024 collapse showed sellers' books can be trapped inside a vendor.
revenue_model: $1,500 buyer-paid report or $995 broker pre-certification per listing, plus a $250 lender-portal fee. Roughly 3 CPA hours per pack plus software gives about 65% gross margin.
non_obvious_insight: The deal-killer is not the price of diligence, it is that diligence gets redone for every buyer. Certifying the listing once turns a per-buyer cost into a per-listing asset that brokers will pay for because it buys deal certainty. Tax transcripts plus bank feeds are also the only evidence AI cannot cheaply fake.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 freelance ex-QoE CPAs and ask 5 regional business brokers for active listings. Run 10 free packs in exchange for case studies and lender feedback, then charge $995 per listing. Walk the format past 2 SBA Preferred Lenders at community banks so 'lender-accepted' is true by month 3.

title: Fire-Line Readiness Passport for Contract Wildfire Crews
one_liner: A qualifications, equipment-inspection and shift-ticket system for private wildland fire engine and crew owners, built so they are never rejected at check-in or paid late.
customer: Owners of private wildland fire engines, hand crews and water tenders contracted by federal and state agencies (the national association alone represents 300+ contractors). A single rig or crew can gross six figures in a season.
problem: Contract fire resources are dispatched from agency lists and must show current qualifications, red cards, fitness tests, insurance, vehicle and pump inspections and correct rate documentation. A missing or expired item gets the rig rejected or sent home at check-in. Payment then depends on shift tickets being filled out and reconciled correctly. Errors mean holds and weeks of waiting while the owner fronts payroll, fuel and insurance. Most operators run this on paper and text messages.
solution: A mobile passport per crew member and rig. It tracks qualification and training expiry, physical and medical dates, insurance certificates and equipment checklists against the specific contract's rules. It flags what will fail at check-in, generates GPS-and-time-stamped shift tickets in agency format with automated checks against contract rates, and packages payment documents. Later it adds accelerated payment.
why_now: Agencies are leaning heavily on contractors, the national Type 2-IA crew contract cycle continues through 2026-27, and the wildfire workforce and pay rules are shifting. It is late September, so the off-season sales window for 2027 contracts is open and there is time to build an MVP before next season.
revenue_model: $150-400 per engine or crew per month. A 1-2% fee on accelerated payment advances against verified, error-free packets, once the record system proves low rejection rates. Insurance and training referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: In fire contracting, the paperwork is the collateral. The rig-days lost to rejection and the payment delays from ticket errors are the real costs. A system that pre-validates packets against the contract's own rules is trusted by agencies, insurers and factoring companies alike, so it can become the data layer for everything financial in the niche. The market looks small (roughly a thousand firms), but each firm has an unusually high willingness to pay.
first_30_days: Join the national contractor association's conversations and contact owners on state preseason contract lists in Oregon, Idaho, Montana and California. Offer a $750-1,500 'pre-season readiness audit' per rig, mapping each contract's checklist. Use the audits to design the MVP. Sell subscriptions from February for the 2027 season.

title: Supplier-Funded Books for Trade-Credit Customers
one_liner: Regional distributors pay to give each micro-customer done-for-you books, and get a permissioned live view of that customer's credit risk.
customer: Regional wholesale distributors (foodservice, produce, beauty supply, auto parts, building materials, uniform and linen) with 500-10,000 micro accounts on net-30 terms.
problem: Distributors extend trade credit to taquerias, salons and garages on gut feel, and bad debt and slow pay eat margin. Micro-customers keep no books, so there is no data to underwrite against. Ramp and Brex have moved upmarket and no vendor serves this tier. The owners will not pay for bookkeeping themselves.
solution: Every active account gets free, done-for-you books, funded by the distributor. Bank and card feeds are connected, the distributor's own invoices are auto-ingested, and receipts arrive by text or WhatsApp. The customer owns the ledger and can export it any time. With the customer's opt-in, the distributor sees cash coverage, the aging of the customer's other bills and payment-risk flags, and can raise limits or offer early-pay discounts to accounts that look healthy.
why_now: LLM categorization pushes cost per account below about $10 a month. The Fed's 2026 data shows microfirms are cash-tight (22% of applicants got no financing, and nonemployers lean on personal funds). The Bench collapse made data ownership and portability a selling point.
revenue_model: The distributor pays $10-25 per active account per month, justified by bad-debt reduction, shorter DSO and lower churn. Upsells: tax filing, payroll, and early-payment financing with a revenue share.
non_obvious_insight: The micro-business will never pay for bookkeeping, but the party carrying its receivable will. A bad account costs a distributor thousands, while $15 a month is noise. Sponsorship also raises switching costs, so the distributor gets retention for free.
first_30_days: Pick one vertical in one metro, such as a produce or beauty-supply distributor. Get 12 months of invoices and payment history for 100 accounts, then backtest whether simple books-derived signals predict late payment. Sign a paid pilot covering 100 accounts, with success defined as DSO and write-offs.

title: Presence Ledger: Reconstruct Every Trip You Took
one_liner: Ingests flight emails, CBP I-94 history, location exports and passport stamps to produce an evidence-backed, officer-proof travel table for naturalization, green-card retention and tax residency.
customer: Immigration law firms (per-client fee), CPAs and tax preparers serving foreign nationals (Form 8843/substantial presence test), HR mobility teams, and green card holders or naturalization applicants directly.
problem: N-400 applicants must list every trip of 24 hours or more in the past 5 years with exact dates. Almost no one can. Officers compare the list with CBP entry and exit records, and an honest gap or mismatch turns an interview into a good-moral-character or false-testimony problem. Green card holders with long absences risk a presumption of broken continuous residence, and scrutiny of returning residents at ports of entry has risen. The same reconstruction is needed for IRS substantial presence day counts, state tax residency audits, and Schengen/UK day counts. Paralegals spend 1-3 hours per client pulling this together by hand, and it is still wrong.
solution: A consent-based tool that pulls the official CBP I-94 travel history, scans Gmail/Outlook for airline and hotel confirmations, ingests Google Timeline or phone location exports and card transactions, and OCRs photos of passport stamps. It reconciles them into a single timeline with confidence flags, asks the user only about unresolved gaps, and exports (a) an N-400-style trip table with the proof behind each row, (b) day counts for physical presence, substantial presence and Schengen limits, and (c) a warning when a planned trip would cross a risk threshold (for example 180 days, or a trip that would break continuous residence).
why_now: Naturalization is being scrutinized more heavily in 2025-26, with a new civics test, a renewed focus on good moral character and reinstated neighborhood-style inquiries. Border stops of returning residents are up. Remote and hybrid work has multiplied cross-border days and tax exposure. Location data is now easy to export from phones, and LLMs make email and stamp parsing cheap enough for a small team to build in weeks.
revenue_model: $49-79 per case billed to law firms (white-label), $29-49 self-serve for applicants, $12-20 per client for CPAs during tax season, and a $9/month subscription for green card holders who want ongoing day tracking and pre-trip risk checks.
non_obvious_insight: The danger is not the trips you forget but the mismatch between your list and what the government already holds. A trip table with attached proof, pre-reconciled against CBP's own record, changes the tone of an interview. The exact same dataset is what tax audits and residency disputes need, so an immigration wedge opens a much larger tax-residency market with no extra data collection.
first_30_days: Build only the N-400 5-year trip table with I-94 history import plus email parsing. Give it free to 10 immigration firms in exchange for a testimonial and a comparison against their manual tables. Charge $49 from client number 11 on. Post the before/after error rates from real cases. In parallel, offer a $15 8843/substantial-presence day-count report through 5 CPAs who serve OPT/H-1B clients.
